bilingual.notes: OSSE 9/2025 exam matrix has no Praxis content exam for Bilingual Education; a completed degree major OR completion of an approved program is required, plus a PLT pedagogy exam. No language-proficiency exam (e.g., ACTFL OPI) is listed by OSSE; leider-2021 coded languageProficiency=true, so the field is set to null pending a direct SEA confirmation.

eld.notes: DC's canonical SEA term is 'English as a Second Language' (ESL). Praxis 5362 (English to Speakers of Other Languages, score 155) is the required content exam, with PLT or World Languages Pedagogy as the pedagogy exam.

sei.notes: DC recognizes five EL program models for LEAs (dual language, inclusion/collaborative, content-based ESL, sheltered content, newcomer) but does not mandate sheltered English instruction training for all teachers.

history.title: DC adopts the State Seal of Biliteracy
history.description: The DC State Board of Education and OSSE established a Seal of Biliteracy for high-school graduates demonstrating proficiency in English plus one or more additional world languages, making DC one of the earliest adopters in the country.

history.title: EPAA 29(100) document analysis (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021)
history.description: Leider, Colombo & Nerlino published in Education Policy Analysis Archives 29(100) a comprehensive document analysis of every state and DC's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI teacher-credentialing requirements, professional teaching standards mentions, and EL-percentage figures, based on primary SEA sources collected October–December 2019. The 2019 coding of District of Columbia's EL-credentialing landscape is preserved as a temporally-anchored research baseline against which the catalog's later verifications are framed.

history.title: OSSE publishes refreshed Educator Credentialing Exams matrix
history.description: OSSE's September 2025 Educator Credentialing Exams document is the operative exam-requirements reference for DC educator credentials. For ESL it specifies Praxis 5362 (English to Speakers of Other Languages, score 155) plus PLT or World Languages Pedagogy; for Bilingual Education it requires a completed degree major or completion of an approved program plus a PLT pedagogy exam, with no Praxis content exam and no language-proficiency exam listed.
